headline: EU Regulatory Briefing: Digital Passports, CSRD Assurance and ESPR Repairability
summary: The European Commission published technical resources for Digital Product Passport registry integration and draft assurance standards for CSRD reporting. Additionally, consultations on ecodesign repairability rules have opened, while reports indicate the proposed Green Claims Directive may be withdrawn.

items.title: Commission Publishes Technical Resources for Digital Product Passport Registry
items.what: The European Commission published six technical resources to assist companies connecting to the Digital Product Passport registry under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation.
items.meaning: Provides initial technical specifications for IT and product data systems, essential for future digital passport compliance across power tools and equipment.
items.action: Forward technical documentation to IT and compliance teams to assess data system readiness.

sources.title: Commission publishes six technical resources for companies connecting to the digital product passport registry

items.title: Draft CSRD Sustainability Assurance Standards Published
items.what: The European Commission released draft sustainability reporting assurance standards under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive framework.
items.meaning: Clarifies audit requirements for sustainability reporting, directly affecting data collection and verification standards for Chinese supplier supply chains.
items.action: Review draft standards with auditors to refine supplier sustainability data protocols.

sources.title: EU Commission Releases Draft Sustainability Reporting Assurance Standards

items.title: EU Consults on Ecodesign Repairability Rules for Electricals
items.what: The European Commission opened a public consultation gathering evidence on proposed repairability requirements for small electrical equipment.
items.meaning: Signals upcoming mandatory design rules for disassembly, spare part availability, and repair information relevant to power tools and garden equipment.
items.action: Evaluate current spare parts distribution and repair documentation across EU operations.

sources.title: EU seeks evidence on repair rules for small electricals and e-scooters

Fix it, don't bin it: the EU consults on Ecodesign repairability requirements

items.title: Reports Suggest Commission May Withdraw Green Claims Directive Proposal
items.what: Media reports indicate the European Commission plans to abandon the proposed Green Claims Directive, though this is not yet officially declared.
items.meaning: Environmental claims remain subject to general consumer law, but explicit substantiation rules under this specific directive may not proceed.
items.action: Continue auditing product marketing claims against established EU consumer protection standards.
